chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both) that he was asked:

About food in which some of it is mixed with some other, and some is better than some other, he said: 'If they are both seen together, there is no harm, provided that the good does not cover the inferior.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to mix high-quality and low-quality food together in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of *gharar* (uncertainty) in commercial transactions by establishing a visual standard for mixed goods. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on transparency, where permissibility hinges on the buyer's ability to distinguish the superior quality from the inferior, preventing deception when the better portion is not entirely concealed.
